title: fix: keep task replies in their chat and avoid Reef commit-link false positives
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes background task replies going to an old external conversation instead of their originating WebChat, and Reef rejecting ordinary GitHub revision links as secrets.

## User Impact

WebChat task completions stay in WebChat, and mirroring an external send into a transcript no longer changes that transcript’s reply destination. Reef can carry GitHub commit, blob, and tree links without mistaking their revision ID for a credential.

The Reef exception is deliberately syntactic: only the exact 40-hex revision position skips the entropy heuristic. It does not verify that a repository or commit exists or is public, and a synthetic value in that position is indistinguishable locally. Known-credential rules and the model guard still inspect the unchanged full message. No configuration or database migration is needed; saved external routes remain available when explicitly selected or when no captured origin exists.

## Why This Change Was Made

Completion routing discarded a captured internal origin and substituted saved external delivery metadata. Separately, the Gateway send handler treated a transcript-mirror selector as the owner of destination-route persistence. The fixes retain the captured origin and separate destination routing from transcript mirroring.

Reef now distinguishes revision-position IDs from other high-entropy tokens. Whole containing URI-like tokens are recognized first, so query/fragment nesting, apostrophes, Markdown wrappers, and nonhierarchical URI schemes cannot create a broader exemption. Other path segments and message text remain scanned.

## Evidence

- The repaired-head ClawSweeper review found a first-contact mirror regression: a separate missing `sessionKey` could lose its transcript even after successful external delivery. Reproduced through the send handler, real outbound persistence, real transcript mirroring and SQLite readback. The outbound-session owner now uses the existing worker-backed identity-only operation to create a missing mirror, without writing the destination route into it; existing mirror identity and saved delivery metadata remain unchanged. **83 send tests passed in 16.53s**, including missing/existing mirror persistence controls, and **48 outbound-route tests passed**. A fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issue.
- Initial CI found three PR-caused media-routing regressions in `checks-node-changed-compact-small-11` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38028654539/job/114144959682)). Reproduced all three locally; media admission now interprets its internal WebChat sentinel before the shared origin resolver. Interactive WebChat remains internal; internal/inter-session media keeps its explicitly supported saved-route fallback. Existing assertions were unchanged. **78 tests passed** across media lifecycle/preparation/retention and requester-settle dispatch in **88.08s**; fresh independent P0–P2 autoreview, core production types, scoped type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace checks passed for the correction.
- **ClawSweeper compatibility-proof disposition:** its initial completed review found no discrete defect and requested stable-to-candidate database proof. This PR changes routing selection, not the stored data model: session delivery types, schema, reader/normalizer and `updateSessionLastRoute` storage representation are unchanged. The subsequent mirror repair extends the existing outbound-session owner with its existing worker-backed `ensure-identity` operation; it adds no storage format or migration. Existing canonical saved external records are consumed in the dispatch regression, including explicit external and missing-origin controls; the send-handler boundary proves destination-route writes remain success-gated and distinct from mirroring. The media CI regression above is repaired at its provenance-aware admission owner. ClawSweeper withdrew that database-upgrade requirement in its next review. These focused boundary proofs cover the changed invariant; no database migration or new storage representation exists to qualify. A stable-version upgrade/E2E was not run and is not claimed.

- Reproduced the wrong-route behavior through requester-settle dispatch and Gateway send handlers before repair; explicit external and shared-main controls remain covered.
- **257 routing/delivery tests passed** across send, completion delivery, settle dispatch/watch, and private-parent completion. Combined initial routing/protocol invocation: **125.17s**; the final, disjoint Reef protocol suite passed **80 tests in 9.83s**.
- The exact original 906-byte rejected reply now passes deterministic checks. Protocol tests exercise outbound sealing, inbound acceptance, guard deny/review, credentials beside links, and nested-URI negative controls.
- Independent P0–P2 autoreview completed with no remaining actionable findings after its two parser findings were reproduced and corrected.
- Core production types, all 27 core-test type shards, Reef package-boundary types, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace, source line-cap and mock-export guards passed in scoped validation.
- **Validation gaps:** aggregate changed checks stop at an unchanged environment-variable budget mismatch (456 names versus 455), reproduced against the unchanged index. One earlier source-selector invocation crashed; the final invocation reached the inherited budget failure. The isolated announce-format E2E runner could not establish managed-Gateway artifact separation and rejected its fallback image/runtime combination before tests. No live peer messages were sent. Final-head CI passed for `dcf20447407204d302bf01ed56fa36b70a5cb250` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38030557217)); both required CI-gate surfaces passed before native squash admission.

<details>
<summary>Changed-test cost</summary>

Measured with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on this host:

| Test file | Wall time |
| --- | ---: |
| `extensions/reef/protocol/checks-ulid.test.ts` | 1.93s |
| `extensions/reef/protocol/pipeline.test.ts` | 2.15s |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts` | 16.53s final (61.47s original cold run) |
| `src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-dispatch.test.ts` | 14.17s |

The existing Gateway send file’s import/preparation and channel-lifecycle coverage dominate its wall time; the original mocked routing cases run in 2–3ms each; the real SQLite mirror cases take 1.87s and 1.07s, with no per-test Gateway boot. The new test-support file runs through this existing suite. Initial CI bundled the media failure family with six other invocations: that failed Node test step took 145.70s (no per-added-case CI allocation is claimed). Final-head CI run 38030557217 completed successfully; prior-head passes remain historical evidence.

</details>
